taxonomy.subtopic: Autoantibodies to alpha-3 type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes

questions.stem_html:
A 24-year-old man develops hemoptysis, fatigue, and rapidly rising creatinine after a respiratory infection. Urinalysis shows dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts. Kidney biopsy demonstrates crescent formation, and immunofluorescence shows smooth linear IgG staining along glomerular capillary loops.

Which antigen is targeted by the pathogenic antibody?

options.text_html: The phospholipase A2 receptor on podocyte membranes
The noncollagenous domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen
Double-stranded DNA within circulating immune complexes
The alpha subunit of the acetylcholine receptor

questions.explanation_html: Anti-GBM antibodies bind the alpha-3 chain noncollagenous domain of type IV collagen shared by glomerular and alveolar basement membranes. Direct binding produces linear IgG and pulmonary-renal disease. The linear staining pattern indicates antibody binding to a uniformly distributed intrinsic basement-membrane antigen.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: PLA2R antibodies are associated with primary membranous nephropathy and granular subepithelial deposits.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Anti-dsDNA immune complexes cause lupus nephritis with granular rather than linear immunofluorescence.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: PR3-ANCA is associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis, a pauci-immune vasculitis.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Acetylcholine-receptor antibodies cause myasthenia gravis, not pulmonary-renal basement-membrane disease.

questions.educational_objective: Identify anti-GBM disease by pulmonary hemorrhage, crescentic nephritis, linear IgG, and antibodies to the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen.
